targeting.title: Gemini in Chrome Not Showing? The 8 Checks Chrome Runs
targeting.metaTitle: Gemini in Chrome Not Showing? 8 Checks to Run
targeting.metaDescription: Gemini in Chrome not showing? Chrome hides the Ask Gemini button unless device, language, sign-in, age, country and admin checks all pass. Check each one.
targeting.excerpt: Why the Ask Gemini button is missing in Chrome, checked against the Chrome 158 source code and Google's help pages: the eight conditions Chrome tests, the 187 supported countries, the languages that are left out, and what to do about each.
targeting.keywords: gemini in chrome not showing, gemini not showing in chrome, gemini not showing up in chrome, gemini in chrome not showing in settings, gemini in chrome not working, how to enable gemini in chrome, gemini in chrome not available, ask gemini button missing chrome, gemini in chrome not showing mac, gemini in chrome not showing linux, gemini in chrome not showing uk, gemini in chrome supported countries
targeting.summary: The Ask Gemini button appears only when eight conditions pass: a supported device, a supported Chrome language, a normal window, a signed-in Chrome, an account that is old enough, a supported country, no administrator block and a pinned button|On 23 November 2026 the list had 187 countries and territories for adults and 43 for users under 18, with no EU member state, and it matches the list in the Chrome 158 source code exactly|The Gemini in Chrome page in Settings appears only after opt-in, and flags or edits to the Local State file do not change the result of the checks
targeting.author: Ali Rehman

siteAnalysis.viewCounter: The stored counter is sampled. src/app/api/views/[slug]/route.ts adds a weight sent by the browser, and all stored values are multiples of 3, so one counted view stands for about three engaged visits of ten seconds or more. A post with 0 can still have had one or two visits. The whole site gained 9 counted views between 22 and 23 November, on three posts from May to July.
siteAnalysis.finding: Among posts published since October, only one keeps gaining views: 'Gemini not showing in Google Docs or Gmail' (42 on 17 November, 45 on 19 November, 51 on 23 November). The three Ollama posts from 18, 19 and 22 November and most n8n posts from November show 0. This article is therefore a sibling of the one recent post with a measurable pull: the same product family, the same kind of problem (a Google AI button that is missing because of eligibility), and a mainstream audience instead of a developer niche.

siteAnalysis.cannibalization: Post 236 covers Gemini inside Docs, Sheets and Gmail (Workspace plan, Smart features, account language, admin switches). Post 128 is a general Gemini guide and post 201 compares AI browsers. None covers the Ask Gemini button of the Chrome browser, its country and language lists, Chrome sign-in, Chrome policies or flags. The new article links to 236 in its third paragraph to send Workspace readers there.

rejectedCandidates.reason: Three dedicated recent guides already lead the result page (stackmatix, needsomefun, two from seoptimate), and I found no primary source beyond one help page to add.
The codes are not documented by Google, so nothing could be verified. Several dedicated pages already exist (thinkfacility, felloai, zerlo, izoate, ultimatewb).
The site's similar post on Copilot in Excel (post 234) has 6 counted views, a weaker signal than the Gemini post.
The last three Ollama posts and most November n8n posts show 0 counted views. Too early to judge them, but no evidence to add a fourth today.

competitors.method: Fetched HTML, main article text only. Term coverage is a keyword presence check, not a quality score.

pages.strength: The strongest page. Written by a long-time Chrome specialist, follows Google's help page closely, has a video, clear signs for each cause, and a 'what does not fix it' list.
pages.missing: No country names or counts, nothing on the EU, no under-18 list, no language names, no explanation of why an update or a restart changes the country, no policy name, no Linux, no source code. It says a missing Settings entry is a sign of a region or language problem; in Chrome 158 the page is shown only after opt-in.

pages.strength: Long and broad; mentions Linux, VPN, admin blocks and the stored country.
pages.missing: Recommends forcing flags (one of which does not exist in Chrome 158) and editing the Local State file. No sources.
The whole article is a Local State edit (is_glic_eligible and the country code). It does not cover eligibility at all.
No country, language, device, policy or update information.

pages.strength: Reports a Mac workaround from users.
pages.missing: About the Gemini app on Mac more than Chrome; no eligibility rules.

notReadable: Four Google community threads (their text is loaded by script)
competitors.gap: No page names the countries or says how many there are, states that no EU country is on the list, separates the adult and under-18 lists, names the languages that are left out, explains how Chrome stores its country and why Google's advice to update Chrome follows from that, shows the policy value to look for, says that the Settings page appears only after opt-in, or checks any of it against Chrome's source code. chromestory is the page to beat for clarity; this article does not try to out-write it on the basics and instead adds the facts it lacks.

images.origin: Original ByteVerse illustrations rendered from SVG with sharp. The cover is a title card with a drawn browser toolbar, not a screenshot. The inline diagram lists the eight checks and was reviewed against the source code and the help pages. No stock photography and no Google logos.

validation.wordCountNote: proseWords is the site's reading-time count and includes the text inside the table.
validation.sourceService: Chromium source read through chromium.googlesource.com (Gitiles) at the tag of the stable release.
validation.stableVersionCheck: docs/content-research/2026-11-23-chrome-version-history.json: Google's version history service listed 158.0.8127.37 at fraction 1 on the stable channel for Windows and Mac on 23 November 2026. Other versions (157.0.8103.79 to .81, 158.0.8127.36, 159.0.8154.13) were served to parts of the same channel.
validation.listComparison: The test script parses the country codes from glic_enabling.h and the locale codes from glic_enabling.cc and compares them with the lists on Google's availability page: 187 adult countries and territories, 43 under-18 countries, 51 languages. The country lists are identical. In the code, Basque, Galician, Icelandic and Zulu are ChromeOS-only; the help page marks only Zulu.
validation.handsOn: docs/content-research/2026-11-23-chrome-hands-on.json, produced by scripts/research-chrome-hands-on-2026-11-23.mjs on Windows 11 Pro with the installed Chrome and empty temporary profiles that were not signed in and were deleted afterwards. The real Chrome profile was not opened. Starting Chrome made its updater download version 158.0.8127.37, which was left pending for the next relaunch.
validation.notTested: A signed-in account, an account under 18, a managed browser, macOS, ChromeOS, Linux, Android and iOS were not tested. What happens after opt-in, and the anchored error state, come from reading the code. Default lists in the code can be overridden by Google's servers.
validation.faqSchemaNote: Six FAQs are visible; the site-wide FAQPage JSON-LD uses the first five.
